text: Within panpsychist frameworks, the 'combination problem' refers to the difficulty of explaining:
choices: Why consciousness emerges only in sufficiently complex brains
How many micro-experiences combine to form a single unified macro-experience
How the universe's single experience divides into individual minds
Why any physical process is accompanied by experience at all
explanation: The combination problem asks how the many micro-experiences posited by panpsychism combine into one unified macro-experience (how roughly 10^27 particles' micro-feels become a single conscious moment). Why any experience arises at all is the hard/emergence problem; emergence-only-in-brains is emergentism; and the universe's experience dividing into individuals is cosmopsychism's mirror-image decombination problem.
